children: Wall Street's major averages were higher on Friday, as the S&P 500 (SP500) and the Nasdaq (COMP:IND) led the rise in an attempt to recover from a persistent technology-led selloff.
The benchmark S&P 500 (
) was last +1%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite
was +1.7%, and the blue-chip Dow
AI-related stocks such as Advanced Micro Devices
, Sandisk
, Micron Technology
, and Dell Technologies
rose after days of declines.
On the economic front, nonfarm payrolls surged in October, sending the unemployment rate

“The 2026 job market is a lot better than last year. It's not perfect. But there are more job opportunities and more industries hiring,” said Heather Long, chief economist at the Navy Federal Credit Union.

“The manufacturing gains were concentrated in the sectors that scream data centers. Construction in residential nosedived -15K. Canary in coalmine is Leisure and Hospitality falling -13K, mostly in accommodations and food,” added Dan Alpert, executive chairman at Westwood Capital.

“The tech-related jobs (both goods and services) are driving hourly wages higher on average (up 0.37% in October), while hours are flat. Notable upward revisions over the past two months aggregating 84,000 jobs leave us with a bullish print, but concentration concerns,” he said.
Over to the bond market, yields rose after the jobs report. The 10-year Treasury yield (
) rose 2 basis points to 4.86%, while the 2-year Treasury yield (
) also rose 5 basis points to 4.52%. The 30-year Treasury yield
was unchanged at 5.26%.
Oil prices were mostly unchanged. Crude oil futures
were $90, while Brent
was $97 per barrel.
The U.S. dollar
rose 0.6%.
